directoryStems.mcq-ef7ef05db46ea9b5640e1705: A 72-year-old woman with osteoporosis and a previous vertebral compression fracture has been sedentary for years because she fears falling. She has no cardiac symptoms, normal vital signs, and takes calcium and vitamin D. What is an appropriate initial approach to exercise?
directoryStems.mcq-9f43ae2434e2d8bbe6bef613: A 78-year-old man with NYHA class II heart failure, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment wants to begin exercising. He lives alone, has fallen twice in the past year, and takes metformin, lisinopril, and metoprolol. His daughter is concerned about safety. Which approach best applies Hazzard's exercise principles?
directoryStems.mcq-3768240064f33676df07868d: A 69-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease and hypertension takes several medications and plans to begin a walking program. What medication-related preparation does Hazzard recommend?
directoryStems.mcq-8eb8a18021db101dfe15cbd9: An 82-year-old man had a stroke six months ago and has mild residual left-sided weakness and fear of falling. He wants to improve strength and balance but worries about his limitations. His wife is supportive and also concerned about safety. Which program design follows the adherence strategies described by Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-6ac81ad456229f54ada964e7: A 76-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and mild frailty has completed eight weeks of low-intensity exercise. Mood and sleep have improved, but strength gains have been small. Her daughter proposes more intensive exercise. Which principle should guide the discussion?
directoryStems.mcq-67980bd8060789a680d43cfb: An 84-year-old woman has been sedentary for years because of arthritis pain. She wants to be stronger for her granddaughter's wedding in six months, has realistic expectations, and has family support. Which educational approach is supported for increasing activity?
directoryStems.mcq-5435ddf7ed1349907da90cee: A 79-year-old man with mild dementia (MMSE 24/30) lives with his family and attends a community exercise program. His daughter says he enjoys the social contact but sometimes forgets the routine between sessions. The program director asks how to support continued participation. Which approach matches Hazzard’s exercise-adherence recommendations?
directoryStems.mcq-e5a122a135df7800d6b5005f: A 67-year-old woman with stable heart failure can walk for ten minutes at a time but becomes fatigued during longer sessions. She requests a plan suited to her current exercise tolerance. Which approach is consistent with the chapter?
directoryStems.mcq-3b114eff8791138b72cc15e0: An 88-year-old man after a stroke participates in supervised low-intensity exercise. He adheres to the program and reports functional improvement, but his illnesses limit vigorous activity. Which principle should guide continued exercise?
directoryStems.mcq-a7b7fe396adc5d08d483c3b4: A 67-year-old woman at her annual visit reports being sedentary during office work and television viewing. She feels overwhelmed about starting exercise. She asks whether she could accumulate activity in short bouts instead of one longer continuous session. Assuming similar total energy expenditure, what does Hazzard report about coronary heart disease risk reduction?

highlightAliases.old: Training trials report changes in bone mineral density that are often small: the chapter describes average increases generally in the range of 1–3%.
highlightAliases.new: In postmenopausal women, training trials compared with no-exercise controls report changes in bone mineral density that are often small: the chapter describes average increases generally in the range of 1–3%, with gains up to 5%.
